messages:
Alex Chen: heads up — trivy-orchestrator started throttling around 18:12 UTC, queue length spiked and prometheus scrape errors increased. also seeing KMS decrypt failures from scanner workers.
Samir Patel: can you paste the worker logs / timeframe? which cluster?
Alex Chen: cluster: prod-infer, namespace: scanner. time window ~18:10-18:30. excerpt: 

``n
2026-03-18T18:14:22Z ERROR worker/scan.go:312 failed to decrypt key: KMS_DECRYPT_FAILED: access denied
2026-03-18T18:14:22Z WARN orchestrator/scheduler.go:89 backoff triggered for worker=42 reason=rate_limit
2026-03-18T18:15:01Z ERROR sync/suppression.go:47 failed to fetch org suppression rules: 503 Service Unavailable
```

ScannerBot: [scan-worker-42] status=failed reason=KMS_DECRYPT_FAILED attempts=3 trace_id=tx-8f3b
Maria Gomez: hm — we pushed an RBAC tweak yesterday for the scanner service account (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4312). maybe the rolebinding lost kms:decrypt on the kms-key resource.
Jess Lee: noticed some suppressed findings resurfacing in GHAS earlier today — repo-level suppressions were fine but org-level suppressions returned findings. could be the suppression-sync job failing as Alex shows.
Ryan O'Neill: +1 on RBAC. quick mitigation: rebind the kms decrypt policy to the scanner SA, and restart affected workers. e.g. 

``
kubectl create rolebinding scanner-kms-decrypt-binding 
  --clusterrole=cloud-kms-decrypt 
  --serviceaccount=scanner:scanner-sa 
  -n scanner || true
kubectl rollout restart deployment/scan-workers -n scanner
```

Samir Patel: if we restart everything now we might flood orchestrator — metrics show we hit max concurrent scans. suggest increasing scheduler backoff and decreasing maxParallelScans to drain the queue gracefully. patch suggestion: 

``
# patch scheduler configmap
kubectl patch configmap trivy-orch-config -n scanner --type merge -p '{"data":{"maxParallelScans":"8","retryBackoffMs":"1200"}}'
```

Alex Chen: applied a quick RBAC bind to restore KMS decrypt perms and restarted a subset of workers. that cleared KMS_DECRYPT_FAILED for the restarted pods but overall queue still ~120 pending. marking for triage.
Samir Patel: I can roll the scheduler change if ops approves. also would like to re-run suppression-sync once service can reach GHAS. command: 

``
kubectl exec -n scanner job/suppression-sync -- /app/sync --target ghas --org redwood
```

Maria Gomez: opening a vuln-triage ticket for any findings that resurfaced due to sync gap. include CVE examples and patch prioritization. preliminary: CVE-2025-1234 (dependency X): low exploitability internally but affects auth flow plugins -> P1 to patch in gateway components; CVE-2026-0456 (yaml-parsing lib): high exploitability in CI runners -> P0 for immediate patch + forced rebuilds.
Jess Lee: please also include a note to validate suppression mapping: repo vs org-level precedence. we saw duplicates where repo-level suppressed but org-level showed as active. add a unit test for suppression-sync.
Alex Chen: created incident INC-3421 and attached logs + runbook. plan: (1) scheduler config bump to prevent further overload (Samir) (2) full RBAC audit of scanner SA + reapply correct rolebindings (Maria, Ryan) (3) re-run suppression-sync and reconcile DB entries (Jess) (4) triage resurfaced findings and prioritize patches (security team).
ScannerBot: suppression-sync job completed: job/suppression-sync finished successfully in 00:01:42. synced=128 suppressed=102 active_new=26
Samir Patel: rolled scheduler patch in prod-infer, decreased maxParallelScans to 6 and increased backoff. queue is draining, pending -> 34 in last 12m.
Maria Gomez: performed RBAC audit and fixed two stale rolebindings. leaving notes in PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4321
Jess Lee: opened a vuln-triage card VTR-889 with list of resurfaced items and prioritized actions. assigning to Samir + Maria.
Alex Chen: thanks all. setting incident status to monitoring. follow-up retrospective tomorrow 10:00am PT. :thumbsup:
